text: God described creation in one chapter. He spent seven chapters describing the tabernacle, a picture of His Son and redemption.
explanation:
The whole universe gets a single chapter in Genesis. But when Moses went up Sinai for forty days and nights, God spent seven chapters, Exodus 25 to 31, describing the ark, the table, the lampstand, the altars, the priest's garments: every one of them a picture of Jesus and His work.

And notice when Moses received the tablets of stone: "at the end of forty days and forty nights." The law came on the last day. For the forty days before that, God's heart was full of His Son. If you want to see what delights God most, look at Jesus.

text: Blue, purple, scarlet: always in that order. Heaven's blue and earth's red meet in the purple of a King.
explanation:
Blue is the colour of heaven: Jesus came from above, and His words and touch carried something heavenly. Scarlet speaks of blood and suffering, of Adam (whose name means red), and of Israel's kings, which is why the soldiers mocked Jesus in a scarlet robe as "King of the Jews." Purple was the colour of Gentile emperors.

Set blue and red side by side and they clash. Put purple between them and the eye rests. And purple is what you get when you blend blue and red. In Jesus, heaven and earth meet in one Person: fully God, fully man, and King of kings.

text: In Jesus' empty tomb, two angels sat at the head and the feet, just like the two cherubim facing each other over the mercy seat.
explanation:
The cherubim on the ark guarded God's holiness; the first cherubim in Scripture held a flaming sword at Eden's gate. Yet on the ark they faced each other, looking down at the mercy seat, where the high priest sprinkled blood once a year. Seeing the blood, they were satisfied: judgment had been carried out.

On resurrection morning, Mary looked into the tomb and saw two angels in white, "one at the head and the other at the feet, where the body of Jesus had lain." The real Mercy Seat. And they were sitting, because the work was finished. God now speaks to you from the mercy seat, not the judgment seat.

text: Every time you come to God, He never says, "You again?"
explanation:
In the tabernacle, twelve loaves, one for each tribe, sat on a golden table before the Lord. It was His bread, His table. God finds His satisfaction in His people coming near to Him. After Jesus had spent time with a broken woman at a well, He told His disciples, "I have food to eat of which you do not know." Blessing her had fed Him.

The table had a golden rim, a crown, all around it, so nothing could fall off. You don't wear out God's welcome by coming too often or asking too much. Heaven is full of unclaimed blessings. Come.

text: God described the ark, table and lampstand first, but held back the altar of incense until after the high priest. No priest, no intercession.
explanation:
In the holy place stood three pieces of furniture: the table of showbread, the lampstand and the golden altar of incense. When God described the tabernacle to Moses, He covered the first two right after the ark, then moved on to curtains, the high priest's garments and the priests' consecration. Only in chapter 30 did He mention the altar of incense.

The incense rose to God as fragrant intercession, and there's no intercession without a priest to offer it. Today Jesus is that High Priest, and "He always lives to make intercession" for you, presenting you to the Father as a sweet fragrance.

text: The burnt offering was killed on the north side of the altar, the direction Israel's invaders always came from.
explanation:
"He shall kill it on the north side of the altar before the Lord." In Israel's geography, enemies and destructive winds came from the north; "out of the north calamity shall break forth." God placed the death of the Lamb right where trouble comes in.

Whatever your need, start at the cross. He became poor so you could be rich. He bore your sicknesses and carried your pains. He was forsaken by lover and friend so you would never be alone. Even when the Shepherd was struck and His sheep scattered, it was so yours would stay together. Every need was met there.

text: "May He accept your burnt sacrifice." The Hebrew word for accept means to reduce to ashes. Ashes mean the fire has finished.
explanation:
On the east side of the altar, the entrance side, was the place for the ashes. Picture a worshipper who offered a lamb yesterday, then went home and started doubting: "Did I do it right? Are my sins really forgiven?" Next morning, as the sun rose in the east, the first thing its light fell on was the ashes. All that was left of yesterday's lamb: proof the judgment was finished.

The Hebrew word for ashes, deshen, also means fatness, abundance. When you come to God, come by the east gate. Remember the ashes. Your sins aren't merely covered; the fire has burned out on Jesus, and there's abundance in the finished work.
